formTitle: Consolidated General Application Form for Immigrant Visa
checkoutEligibleNote: Not yet decided -- same open business-classification question as the other mapped forms. This mapping covers field-level automation only; checkout eligibility is a separate business decision.
reproductionRightsNote: Confirmed directly on the form itself: 'THIS DOCUMENT MAY BE REPRODUCED AND IS NOT FOR SALE', printed at the top of both pages.
derivedFrom: Measured from 300 DPI rasters of both pages of the real original PDF (downloaded from the private fis-bi-forms-library R2 bucket, originals/BOC04.QF.001.pdf), a Microsoft Word export with a standard (0,0)-origin MediaBox. A third distinct template family within this library: every applicant-facing field (not just dates) is rendered as a comb-grid of individual character cells, with a form-wide uniform cell pitch of 12.96pt (independently confirmed across multiple unrelated fields -- Present Immigration Status, Last Name, Other Name(s)/Alias(es) -- via direct pixel measurement, then used to auto-generate colsPt for every field from just its outer left/right bounds, rather than measuring every internal divider by hand). Date fields use the same DD-MMM-YYYY 3-group (2+3+4 cell) convention already established for ARD04.QF.003, each group its own charBoxFields entry.

measurementNotes.uniformCellPitchDiscovery: The first two fields measured (Present Immigration Status, Last Name) independently converged on a ~12.96pt cell pitch via direct column-divider pixel detection. This was then used as a form-wide constant: for every other field, only the box's outer left/right/top/bottom bounds were measured directly, and colsPt was generated as evenly-spaced points between them (cell count = round(width/12.96)) -- cutting the per-field measurement burden roughly in half versus measuring every internal divider by hand, while still deriving every coordinate from the real original PDF, never estimated from memory.
measurementNotes.checkboxPositionCorrection: Checkboxes on this form sit noticeably closer to their row's own label text than on the Word-template forms mapped previously (IRD04.QF.004) -- an initial x-range guess based on the printed label's own text position caught only stray anti-aliased text pixels and returned no clean border. Corrected by a pixel-ruled visual-grid overlay crop (Type of Visa Application / Method of Application rows) that located the true checkbox bounds directly, after which Sex and Civil Status used the same corrected-range approach from the start.
measurementNotes.landlineMobilePairsNotSharedBorder: Unlike the row-shared-bottom-line style seen on ADM05.QF.001, this form's Landline/Mobile field pairs (Section III contact info, Character References, Petitioner section) are two fully independent boxes with their own top and bottom borders and a label line in between -- confirmed by direct visual crop after an initial assumption (based on the otherAlias1/otherAlias2 and spouseAlias1/spouseAlias2 pairs elsewhere on this same form, which DO share a border) proved wrong for this specific field pair.
measurementNotes.childDateOfBirthIsThreeGroupsNotOneComb: child1Dob/child2Dob initially measured as a single outer-bounds comb (coincidentally yielding a plausible-looking 11-cell count, since the combined width of the real 2+3+4-cell groups plus their two inter-group gaps is close to 11 cells). A pixel-ruled visual crop showed this was wrong: each is the same 3-group DD-MMM-YYYY structure (2+3+4 cells, with gaps) as every other date field on this form, not one continuous comb -- corrected to match, with column positions matching the ACR section's own date fields on page 2 almost exactly (confirming this x-position is a reused template row, not coincidence).
measurementNotes.claimStubAndRepresentativeBlockNotPopula: The 'APPLICANT'S ACR I-CARD CLAIM STUB' (bottom of page 1: Applicant's Name, ACR Number, Visa Type) and the back-page 'Name of Representative / Accredited Travel Agency / BI Accreditation No. / Contact No. / Residential-Office Address / Signature' block (very bottom of page 2, used only when an authorized representative physically claims the printed ACR I-Card) are both claim-time, BI-counter-completed sections, not part of the online application itself -- consistent with the same treatment already given to ADM05.QF.001's own Claim Stub. Neither is mapped as a fillable field; both are excluded from customer-audience output structurally (no charBoxFields/checkboxFields reference them), not via cropping.
measurementNotes.acrSectionTreatedAsCustomerOptional: Section V's ACR Number/Date of Issuance/Expiry/CRN fields (left column) are NOT under the form's own 'DO NOT FILL OUT THIS PORTION' label (which covers only the right-column Application Number/Received-Recommended-by/Reviewed-by/Approved-by block) -- they are for an applicant who already holds a prior ACR I-Card to declare it, so they are mapped as ordinary, optional ('N/A' if inapplicable) customer fields, consistent with the same treatment given to ACR/SSRN fields on ARD04.QF.003 and IRD04.QF.004.
measurementNotes.visualInspectionCorrections: Caught via rendering the real test PDF and visually inspecting every field (not just a successful CLI run), as required: (1) Section III Landline/Mobile xStart was mismeasured at 48.24pt, overlapping the 'Landline'/'Mobile' row labels with the first 3 of 15 drawn cells -- a pixel-divider scan against the real original showed the box actually starts at 87.48pt (12 cells, ending at 243.0pt, matching the Mobile row exactly), corrected accordingly. (2) The Height [cm] field was originally measured with only 3 boundary points (2 cells), causing a genuine 3-character sample value ('165') to show an overflow/truncation warning -- a pixel-divider scan showed the real box has 4 dividers (3 cells, starting at 87.48pt, not 100.68pt), so the first cell had simply been missed; corrected to the full 3-cell box, which resolves the overflow entirely (no longer a genuine form limitation).

signatureBlock.note: Wet-ink signatures and date required by the official form -- this form uniquely requires THREE wet-ink elements (Date, Petitioner's Signature, Applicant's Signature), unlike every other mapped form's two. Deliberately left blank -- not populated by this automation. The inline consent-paragraph name blanks ('I, ___, personally or through my agent/representative ___') on page 2 follow the same policy and are not separately mapped.

petitionerSignatureLine.note: Extra, form-specific: this form requires the PETITIONER's own wet-ink signature in addition to the applicant's, distinct from the schema's required signatureLine (the applicant's own). Positioned between the Date and Applicant's Signature columns.

customerPreviewCropBox.note: No separate BI-internal static header/footer region exists on this form -- the Claim Stub, the back-page Representative block, and the staff-only Application Number/Received-Reviewed-Approved section are all excluded from customer-audience output structurally (none are mapped as charBoxFields/checkboxFields at all, or -- for Application Number -- via roles.visibleTo), not via region cropping. The full page is therefore the customer preview region for both pages. This single-region box describes ONE page's own bounds (used by consumers that only expect a single crop box); the two real pages' own full-page regions are declared separately in customerVisibleRegions below, since this is the engine's first genuinely multi-page form.

customerVisibleRegions.note: Two regions, the full extent of each of the form's two real PDF pages (not a same-page staff-only split like 2014-13-006's two regions) -- see customerPreviewCropBox note. The composited customer preview therefore shows both full pages stacked, with a plain page-break divider (no 'FIS staff prepare the remaining sections' caption, since nothing is hidden -- see raster-pipeline.js/svg-compose.js's own comments on this distinction).
